questions.question: What number comes next? 5, 9, 13, 17, ___
questions.explanation: Each term adds 4: 17 + 4 = 21.

questions.question: What number comes next? 2, 6, 18, 54, ___
questions.explanation: Each term is multiplied by 3: 54 × 3 = 162.

questions.question: What number comes next? 3, 4, 7, 11, 18, 29, ___
questions.explanation: Each term is the sum of the two before it: 18 + 29 = 47.

questions.question: What number comes next? 10, 3, 12, 6, 14, 9, ___
questions.explanation: Two series alternate. Odd positions: 10, 12, 14, 16 (+2). Even positions: 3, 6, 9 (+3). The 7th term continues the first series: 16.

questions.question: What letter comes next? B, E, I, N, ___
questions.explanation: Positions are 2, 5, 9, 14: the gaps grow +3, +4, +5. Next is +6, so 14 + 6 = 20 = T.

questions.question: PETAL : FLOWER :: PAGE : ___
questions.explanation: A petal is a part of a flower; a page is a part of a book (part-to-whole).

questions.question: THERMOMETER : TEMPERATURE :: BAROMETER : ___
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature; a barometer measures air (atmospheric) pressure.

questions.question: DRIZZLE : DOWNPOUR :: BREEZE : ___
questions.explanation: A downpour is a much stronger drizzle; a gale is a much stronger breeze (degree relationship).

questions.question: Which pair shows the same relationship as SURGEON : SCALPEL?
questions.explanation: A scalpel is a cutting tool a surgeon uses; a knife is a cutting tool a chef uses. A canvas is a surface and a novel is a product, not tools.

questions.question: All the mangoes in the basket are ripe. This fruit is a mango from the basket. Which statement must be true?
questions.explanation: Every mango in the basket is ripe, and this is a mango from the basket, so it must be ripe. Sweetness is never stated.

questions.question: If it rains, the game is cancelled. The game was NOT cancelled. What can be concluded?
questions.explanation: This is the contrapositive: if the game was not cancelled, then it did not rain.

questions.question: Ana is taller than Ben. Carlo is shorter than Ben. Dina is taller than Ana. Who is the shortest?
questions.explanation: From tallest to shortest: Dina > Ana > Ben > Carlo.

questions.question: Some students are athletes. All athletes are disciplined. Which conclusion is valid?
questions.explanation: The students who are athletes must be disciplined, so at least some students are disciplined. Nothing is known about the other students.

questions.question: An arrow points north. It is rotated 90° clockwise, then 180°. Which way does it point now?
questions.explanation: 90° clockwise turns north to east. Another 180° turns east to west.

questions.question: A cube net has four squares in a row labeled 1, 2, 3, 4. Square 5 is attached above square 2, and square 6 below square 2. When folded into a cube, which face is opposite square 2?
questions.explanation: The row of four wraps around the cube, so faces two apart are opposite: 1 and 3, 2 and 4. Faces 5 and 6 are opposite each other.

questions.question: Which word looks exactly the same when seen in a mirror placed beside it (a left-right reflection)?
questions.explanation: A left-right mirror reverses the letter order and flips each letter. MOM is a palindrome AND M and O are symmetric left-to-right. B, N, D and E are not symmetric, so they appear flipped.

questions.question: If today is Wednesday, what day will it be 10 days from now?
questions.explanation: Days repeat every 7. 10 = 7 + 3, so count 3 days after Wednesday: Saturday.

questions.question: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand at 3:30?
questions.explanation: Angle = |30H − 5.5M| = |30(3) − 5.5(30)| = |90 − 165| = 75°. The hour hand has moved halfway between 3 and 4.

questions.question: Liza is 4 years older than Marco. In 5 years, the sum of their ages will be 40. How old is Marco now?
questions.explanation: Let Marco = m. In 5 years: (m + 5) + (m + 4 + 5) = 40, so 2m + 14 = 40 and m = 13.

questions.question: At a meeting, each of 8 people shakes hands with every other person exactly once. How many handshakes happen?
questions.explanation: Each person shakes 7 hands, but each handshake involves 2 people: 8 × 7 ÷ 2 = 28.

questions.question: What number comes next? 81, 27, 9, 3, ___
questions.explanation: Each term is divided by 3: 3 ÷ 3 = 1.

questions.question: What number comes next? 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, ___
questions.explanation: The differences are 3, 5, 7, 9, so the next difference is 11: 26 + 11 = 37. (Each term is n² + 1.)

questions.question: What letter comes next? A, C, F, J, O, ___
questions.explanation: Positions are 1, 3, 6, 10, 15: the gaps grow +2, +3, +4, +5. Next is +6, so 15 + 6 = 21 = U.

questions.question: What number comes next? 1, 2, 6, 24, 120, ___
questions.explanation: Multiply by 2, then 3, then 4, then 5. Next multiply by 6: 120 × 6 = 720.

questions.question: What number comes next? 4, 9, 19, 39, 79, ___
questions.explanation: Each term is doubled, then 1 is added: 79 × 2 + 1 = 159.

questions.question: What number comes next? 3, 7, 16, 35, 74, ___
FISH : SCHOOL :: BIRD : ___
questions.explanation: A group of fish is a school; a group of birds is a flock.

questions.question: AUTHOR : BOOK :: COMPOSER : ___
questions.explanation: An author creates a book; a composer creates a symphony (creator to creation).

questions.question: HUNGRY : FAMISHED :: TIRED : ___
questions.explanation: Famished is an extreme degree of hungry; exhausted is an extreme degree of tired. Sleepy is not stronger than tired.

questions.question: SEED : TREE :: EGG : ___
questions.explanation: A seed develops into a tree; an egg develops into a bird. Shell and yolk are parts of the egg.

questions.question: ARCHIPELAGO : ISLAND :: CONSTELLATION : ___
questions.explanation: An archipelago is a group of islands; a constellation is a group of stars.

questions.question: Which pair shows the same relationship as DROUGHT : FAMINE?
questions.explanation: A drought can cause a famine (cause, then effect). An earthquake can cause a tsunami. "Rain : Cloud" and "Smoke : Fire" list the effect first, the reverse order.

questions.question: No reptiles have feathers. A snake is a reptile. Which statement must be true?
questions.explanation: If no reptile has feathers and a snake is a reptile, a snake has no feathers. Scales may be true in real life but are not stated.

questions.question: Ramon finished the race before Sofia. Sofia finished before Tina. Which statement must be true?
questions.explanation: The order is Ramon, then Sofia, then Tina, so Ramon finished before Tina.

questions.question: If a shape is a square, then it is a rectangle. Shape X is not a rectangle. What can be concluded?

options.text: Shape X is not a square.

questions.explanation: By the contrapositive, anything that is not a rectangle cannot be a square. We do not know what shape X actually is.

questions.question: Ella's mother is the only daughter of Carlos. How is Carlos related to Ella?
questions.explanation: Carlos is the father of Ella's mother, which makes him Ella's grandfather.

questions.question: Five friends sit in a row. Ana sits in the middle. Ben sits at the left end. Carla sits right next to Ana, on Ana's right. Dino does not sit next to Ben. Where does Elle sit?
questions.explanation: Seats 1–5 from the left: Ben 1, Ana 3, Carla 4. Seats 2 and 5 remain. Dino cannot sit next to Ben (seat 2), so Dino takes seat 5 and Elle takes seat 2.

questions.question: All doctors in the clinic are licensed. Some licensed people are volunteers. Which conclusion is valid?

options.text: Some doctors in the clinic are volunteers.
No doctor in the clinic is a volunteer.
None of these conclusions necessarily follows.

questions.explanation: The licensed volunteers might or might not be the doctors, so we cannot say some doctors volunteer, or that none do. Nothing is said about all volunteers.

questions.question: A clock's minute hand points at 12. Where does it point after turning 270° clockwise?
questions.explanation: Each 90° is a quarter turn: 12 → 3 → 6 → 9. Three quarter turns (270°) end at 9.

questions.question: Which capital letter looks the same when flipped top to bottom (it has a horizontal line of symmetry)?
questions.explanation: The top and bottom halves of E match across a horizontal line. P, R and J do not.

questions.question: A square sheet of paper is folded in half, then in half again to make a smaller square. One hole is punched through all the layers. How many holes appear when it is unfolded?
questions.explanation: Two folds make 4 layers, and the punch goes through every layer, so there are 4 holes.

questions.question: How many faces does a triangular prism have?
questions.explanation: It has 2 triangular faces (top and bottom) and 3 rectangular side faces: 5 in total.

questions.question: A cube painted red on all faces is cut into 27 equal smaller cubes (3 × 3 × 3). How many small cubes have exactly two red faces?
questions.explanation: Cubes with two painted faces sit in the middle of each edge. A cube has 12 edges, with 1 such cube per edge: 12. (The 8 corner cubes have three red faces.)

questions.question: A cube painted on all faces is cut into 64 equal smaller cubes (4 × 4 × 4). How many small cubes have paint on exactly one face?
questions.explanation: On each face, the cubes not on an edge form a 2 × 2 square (4 cubes). There are 6 faces: 6 × 4 = 24.

questions.question: A jeepney ride costs ₱13. How much do 4 rides cost?
Today is Monday. What day of the week was it 30 days ago?
questions.explanation: 30 = 4 weeks + 2 days. Going back 2 days from Monday gives Saturday.

questions.question: A father is 3 times as old as his son. In 12 years, he will be twice as old as his son. How old is the son now?
questions.explanation: Let the son be s. Then 3s + 12 = 2(s + 12), so 3s + 12 = 2s + 24 and s = 12. Check: 36 + 12 = 48 = 2 × 24.

questions.question: How many minutes are there from 9:45 AM to 1:20 PM on the same day?
questions.explanation: 9:45 AM to 1:45 PM is 4 hours (240 minutes). 1:20 PM is 25 minutes earlier: 240 − 25 = 215.

questions.question: In a class of 40 students, 25 like basketball, 18 like volleyball, and 7 like both. How many like neither sport?
questions.explanation: Students who like at least one sport: 25 + 18 − 7 = 36 (the 7 were counted twice). Neither: 40 − 36 = 4.

questions.question: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand at 7:20?
Choose the word closest in meaning to METICULOUS.
questions.explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail.

questions.question: "Unlike his gregarious sister, who loved parties, Paolo preferred to spend weekends alone." GREGARIOUS most likely means:
questions.explanation: "Unlike" signals a contrast with preferring to be alone, and "loved parties" supports the meaning sociable.

questions.question: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to SCARCE.
questions.explanation: Scarce means in short supply; the opposite is plentiful. Rare and limited are synonyms.

questions.question: Using its word parts, what does CHRONOMETER most likely mean?

options.text: A written account of a life

questions.explanation: chron = time and meter = measuring instrument, so a chronometer measures time.

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: "The box of old photographs ___ in the attic."
questions.explanation: The subject is "box" (singular). "Of old photographs" is a prepositional phrase and does not change the subject.

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: "Neither the coach nor the players ___ happy with the referee's decision."
questions.explanation: With neither/nor, the verb agrees with the closer subject, "players" (plural), so use "were."

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?

options.text: Between you and me, the plan won't work.
Between you and I, the plan won't work.
Between yourself and I, the plan won't work.
Between you and myself, the plan won't work.

questions.explanation: "Between" is a preposition, so it takes the object pronoun "me."

questions.question: Which part of this sentence contains an error? "Everyone in the two sections have finished the reading assignment."
questions.explanation: "Everyone" is singular, so the verb should be "has finished." The phrase "in the two sections" does not make the subject plural.

questions.question: Read: "Mangroves line many coasts in the Philippines. Their tangled roots slow down waves, reducing damage from storm surges, and trap sediment that would otherwise cloud nearby coral reefs. Young fish also shelter among the roots. Despite these benefits, large areas of mangroves have been cleared for fishponds and coastal development." What is the main idea?

options.text: Fishponds are the best use of coastal land.
Coral reefs are cloudy because of young fish.
Mangroves provide important benefits, yet many have been cleared.
Storm surges happen only in the Philippines.

questions.explanation: The passage lists the benefits of mangroves and ends by noting their loss. The other choices are unsupported or misread details.

questions.question: Read: "Mangroves ... trap sediment that would otherwise cloud nearby coral reefs." If a mangrove forest next to a reef were removed, what would most likely happen?

options.text: More sediment would reach the reef, making the water cloudier.
The reef would be better protected from waves.
Nothing would change for the reef.

questions.explanation: The passage says mangroves trap sediment that would otherwise cloud reefs, so removing them would let more sediment reach the reef.

questions.question: "The speaker's remarks were so candid that some officials felt uncomfortable; she openly named the agencies that had failed to act." CANDID most nearly means:
questions.explanation: "Openly named" the agencies shows she spoke frankly and honestly.

questions.question: "Our town's river was once clear enough to swim in. Today, plastic bags cling to its banks. If each household sorted its waste, the river could recover within a few years." What is the author's main purpose?

options.text: To entertain readers with a story about swimming
To persuade readers to change their waste habits
To describe the full history of the town

questions.explanation: The passage contrasts past and present, then proposes an action households should take. That is persuasion.

questions.question: Which of the following is a complete sentence?

options.text: The students waited under the shed.

questions.explanation: "The students waited under the shed" has a subject and verb and expresses a complete thought. The "Because..." and "Although..." choices are dependent clauses, and "Running to catch the jeepney" has no subject or main verb.

questions.question: Which sentence is a comma splice?

options.text: I studied all night, I was tired.
I studied all night, so I was tired.
I studied all night; I was tired.
Because I studied all night, I was tired.

questions.explanation: "I studied all night, I was tired" joins two independent clauses with only a comma. The other choices fix this with "so," a semicolon, or a dependent clause.

questions.question: Which sentence uses correct parallel structure?

options.text: She likes reading, to swim, and bikes.
She likes reading, swimming, and biking.
She likes to read, swimming, and to bike.
She likes read, swim, and biking.

questions.explanation: All three items use the same -ing form.

questions.question: Which sentence has NO dangling or misplaced modifier?

options.text: Walking to school, the rain soaked my uniform.
Soaked by the rain, the school was where I walked.
The rain soaked, walking to school, my uniform.
Walking to school, I got soaked by the rain.

questions.explanation: In "Walking to school, I got soaked," the phrase correctly describes "I." In "Walking to school, the rain soaked my uniform," it wrongly suggests the rain was walking.

questions.question: "The classroom was a zoo after the teacher left." This is an example of:
questions.explanation: It says the classroom WAS a zoo, without "like" or "as." That is a metaphor.

questions.question: "The old jeepney groaned as it climbed the hill." Which figure of speech is used?
questions.explanation: Groaning is a human action given to a vehicle, so it is personification.

questions.question: A fire station burns down. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: The opposite of what you would expect happens: the place meant to fight fires is destroyed by one.

questions.question: Which point of view uses "he," "she," and "they" and lets the narrator reveal the thoughts of ALL the characters?
questions.explanation: An omniscient ("all-knowing") third-person narrator can share every character's thoughts. Third-person limited follows only one character.

questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to ABUNDANT.
questions.explanation: Abundant means existing in large amounts, so plentiful is the closest meaning. Scarce is its opposite.

questions.question: "The candidate's speech was full of vague promises; she never gave specific details." VAGUE most likely means:
questions.explanation: The clue "never gave specific details" shows the promises were not clear or precise.

questions.question: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to CONCEAL.
questions.explanation: Conceal means to hide. Its opposite is reveal, which means to show or make known.

questions.question: In the word PREVIEW, what does the prefix "pre-" mean?
questions.explanation: "Pre-" means before, so a preview is a view of something before it is fully shown.

questions.question: All four words describe someone careful with money. Which one has a NEGATIVE connotation?
questions.explanation: Stingy suggests being unwilling to share or spend, which is a criticism. The other words praise careful spending.

questions.question: "The new policy was met with ambivalence; many employees saw both benefits and drawbacks." AMBIVALENCE means:
questions.explanation: Seeing "both benefits and drawbacks" means holding mixed or conflicting feelings. (ambi- = both)

questions.question: Choose the correct word: "The dog wagged ___ tail."
questions.explanation: "Its" shows possession (the tail belongs to it). "It's" means "it is." "Its'" is never correct.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: "There are ___ students in the library today than yesterday."
questions.explanation: Students can be counted, so use "fewer." "Less" is for amounts that cannot be counted.

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: "Mathematics ___ my favorite subject."
questions.explanation: Subject names like mathematics, physics and economics end in -s but are singular, so they take "is."

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: "She ___ in Manila since 2020."
questions.explanation: "Since 2020" describes an action that started in the past and continues now, which needs the present perfect: "has lived."

questions.question: Choose the correct pronoun: "The award was given to Maria and ___."
questions.explanation: After the preposition "to," use the object pronoun "me." Test it alone: "given to me," not "given to I."

questions.question: Which sentence uses WHO or WHOM correctly in formal English?

options.text: Whom is calling at this hour?
To who should I send this letter?
Whom did you invite to the party?
The girl whom won the contest is my cousin.

questions.explanation: "Whom" is the object of "invite" (you invited HIM, so whom). In the others, "who" is needed as a subject, or "whom" after the preposition "to."

questions.question: Read: "Jose had practiced the piano piece for weeks, but on the day of the recital his hands trembled as he walked onstage. He took a deep breath, remembered his teacher's advice to focus on one measure at a time, and began. By the final chord, the audience was on its feet." How did Jose feel as he walked onstage?
questions.explanation: His trembling hands and the deep breath he needed show that he was nervous.

questions.question: Read: "Jose had practiced the piano piece for weeks, but on the day of the recital his hands trembled as he walked onstage. He took a deep breath, remembered his teacher's advice to focus on one measure at a time, and began. By the final chord, the audience was on its feet." What can be inferred about his performance?
questions.explanation: He played through to the final chord, and the audience rose to its feet, which suggests they appreciated it.

questions.question: A story about a piano recital ends: "By the final chord, the audience was on its feet." The phrase "on its feet" most likely means the audience:
questions.explanation: After a performance, an audience rising "to its feet" is giving a standing ovation.

questions.question: Read: "Bamboo is one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth; some species can grow nearly a meter in a single day. Because it regrows quickly after harvesting, bamboo is often promoted as a sustainable building material. However, untreated bamboo can be damaged by insects and moisture, so it must be properly processed before use." What is the main idea?

options.text: Bamboo grows quickly and can be a sustainable material when properly processed.
Bamboo is the strongest building material.
Insects are the biggest threat to all buildings.
Bamboo should never be used for building.

questions.explanation: The passage covers bamboo's fast growth, its use as a sustainable material, and the need to treat it. The other choices are not supported.

questions.question: Read: "Bamboo is one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth; some species can grow nearly a meter in a single day. Because it regrows quickly after harvesting, bamboo is often promoted as a sustainable building material. However, untreated bamboo can be damaged by insects and moisture, so it must be properly processed before use." The word "However" at the start of the third sentence signals:
questions.explanation: "However" introduces a drawback (insects and moisture) that contrasts with the benefits just described.

questions.question: Read: "Bamboo is one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth; some species can grow nearly a meter in a single day. Because it regrows quickly after harvesting, bamboo is often promoted as a sustainable building material. However, untreated bamboo can be damaged by insects and moisture, so it must be properly processed before use." Which statement would the author most likely agree with?

options.text: Untreated bamboo is ideal for houses.
Every bamboo species grows a meter each day.
Bamboo's usefulness depends partly on how it is prepared.

questions.explanation: The author says bamboo must be properly processed before use. Only "some species" grow nearly a meter a day, and untreated bamboo can be damaged.

questions.question: Choose the best word to complete the sentence: "I wanted to go out; ___, it was raining."
questions.explanation: The rain contrasts with wanting to go out, so the contrast word "however" fits.

questions.question: Which of these is a run-on sentence?

options.text: The rain stopped, and we went outside.
When the rain stopped, we went outside.
The rain stopped we went outside.
The rain stopped; we went outside.

questions.explanation: "The rain stopped we went outside" joins two complete sentences with no punctuation or conjunction. The others use ", and," a dependent clause, or a semicolon.

questions.question: Which sentence is in the ACTIVE voice?

options.text: The cake was baked by Lola.

questions.explanation: In the active voice, the subject does the action: Lola (subject) baked the cake. The others use "was/were + past participle" (passive).

questions.question: Arrange the steps in the most logical order: (1) Then, add the rice and stir. (2) First, heat the oil in a pan. (3) Finally, serve while hot. (4) Next, sauté the garlic until golden.
questions.explanation: The transition words give the order: First (2), Next (4), Then (1), Finally (3).

questions.question: Which sentence is the clearest and most concise?

options.text: In my opinion, I think we should start early.
I personally believe and think we should start early.
I think we should start early.
It is my opinion that I think we should start early.

questions.explanation: "In my opinion," "I think" and "I believe" mean the same thing, so using more than one is redundant. Only one choice avoids the repetition.

questions.question: The writer has only one brother. Which sentence uses commas correctly?

options.text: My brother who lives in Cebu, is a nurse.
My brother, who lives in Cebu is a nurse.
My, brother who lives in Cebu is a nurse.
My brother, who lives in Cebu, is a nurse.

questions.explanation: With only one brother, "who lives in Cebu" is extra (non-essential) information, so it is set off by a PAIR of commas.

questions.question: "The thunder boomed and the rain went pitter-patter on the roof." Which device is used?
questions.explanation: "Boomed" and "pitter-patter" imitate actual sounds, which is onomatopoeia.

questions.question: "Her smile was as bright as the sun." This is an example of:
questions.explanation: It compares her smile to the sun using "as," which makes it a simile.

questions.question: "I've told you a million times to clean your room!" This is an example of:
questions.explanation: "A million times" is an extreme exaggeration for emphasis, which is hyperbole.

questions.question: In a story, a family struggles to survive a strong typhoon. What type of conflict is this?
questions.explanation: The characters struggle against a natural force (the typhoon), so it is character vs. nature, an external conflict.

questions.question: In a play, the audience knows the villain is hiding behind the door, but the hero does not. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Dramatic irony happens when the audience knows something a character does not.

questions.question: The phrase "deafening silence" is an example of:
questions.explanation: An oxymoron puts two contradictory words side by side ("deafening" and "silence"). A paradox is a whole statement that seems contradictory but holds a truth.

questions.question: Solve for x: 3x − 7 = 11
questions.explanation: Add 7 to both sides: 3x = 18. Divide by 3: x = 6.

questions.question: What are the roots of x² − 5x + 6 = 0?
questions.explanation: Factor: (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0, so x = 2 or x = 3.

questions.question: If f(x) = 2x² − 3x + 1, what is f(−2)?
For what positive value of k does x² + kx + 9 = 0 have exactly one real root?
questions.explanation: One real root means the discriminant is 0: k² − 4(1)(9) = 0, so k² = 36 and k = 6.

questions.question: A right triangle has legs of 6 cm and 8 cm. How long is the hypotenuse?
What is the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon?
What is the area of a circle with a diameter of 10 cm?
questions.explanation: The radius is half the diameter: r = 5. A = πr² = 25π cm².

questions.question: In right triangle ABC with the right angle at C, sin A = 3/5. What is tan A?
questions.explanation: Opposite = 3 and hypotenuse = 5, so adjacent = √(25 − 9) = 4. tan A = opposite/adjacent = 3/4.

questions.question: What is the mean of 4, 8, 10, 12, and 16?
questions.explanation: Sum = 50, and there are 5 values: 50 ÷ 5 = 10.

questions.question: What is the median of 7, 3, 9, 1, 5, 11?
questions.explanation: Sorted: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11. With six values, average the two middle ones: (5 + 7) ÷ 2 = 6.

questions.question: A bag has 3 red, 5 blue, and 2 green marbles. One marble is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is NOT blue?
questions.explanation: There are 10 marbles and 5 are not blue (3 red + 2 green): 5/10 = 1/2.

questions.question: How many different 3-member committees can be formed from 7 students?
questions.explanation: Order does not matter, so use combinations: C(7, 3) = 7! / (3! × 4!) = 35. (210 would count different orders.)

questions.question: A shirt originally priced at ₱800 is sold at 25% off. What is the sale price?
₱10,000 is invested at 6% simple interest per year. How much interest is earned after 3 years?
questions.explanation: I = Prt = 10,000 × 0.06 × 3 = ₱1,800. (₱11,800 is the total amount, not the interest.)

questions.question: A bus travels 180 km in 3 hours. At the same speed, how long will it take to travel 300 km?
questions.explanation: Speed = 180 ÷ 3 = 60 km/h. Time = 300 ÷ 60 = 5 hours.

questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 6 hours. Pipe B can fill it in 3 hours. How long will it take if both pipes are used together?
questions.explanation: Together they fill 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2 of the tank per hour, so the full tank takes 2 hours.

questions.question: What is the derivative of f(x) = x⁴?
questions.explanation: Power rule: bring down the 4 and subtract 1 from the exponent: 4x³.

questions.question: Evaluate the limit as x → 2 of (x² − 4) / (x − 2).
questions.explanation: Factor: (x − 2)(x + 2) / (x − 2) = x + 2 for x ≠ 2. Substitute x = 2: 4.

questions.question: If f(x) = 3x² − 4x + 7, what is f′(x)?
questions.explanation: Differentiate term by term: 3x² → 6x, −4x → −4, and the constant 7 → 0.

questions.question: For f(x) = x² − 6x + 5, at what value of x is f(x) at its minimum?
questions.explanation: Set the derivative to 0: f′(x) = 2x − 6 = 0, so x = 3. The parabola opens upward, so this is the minimum.

questions.question: Simplify: 2(x + 3) − 4
questions.explanation: Distribute: 2x + 6. Then subtract 4: 2x + 2.

questions.question: If x + y = 10 and x − y = 4, what is x?
questions.explanation: Add the two equations: 2x = 14, so x = 7 (and y = 3).

questions.question: What is the slope of the line through (1, 2) and (4, 11)?
Simplify: x³ · x⁴
questions.explanation: When multiplying powers with the same base, add the exponents: 3 + 4 = 7.

questions.question: If 2^(x + 1) = 32, what is x?
questions.explanation: 32 = 2⁵, so x + 1 = 5 and x = 4.

questions.question: Solve: |2x − 3| = 7
questions.explanation: Either 2x − 3 = 7 (x = 5) or 2x − 3 = −7 (x = −2). An absolute-value equation usually has two solutions.

questions.question: What is the perimeter of a rectangle 8 cm long and 5 cm wide?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 2(length + width) = 2(8 + 5) = 26 cm. (40 would be the area in cm².)

questions.question: Two angles of a triangle measure 50° and 60°. What is the third angle?
questions.explanation: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°: 180° − 50° − 60° = 70°.

questions.question: What is the volume of a cylinder with radius 3 cm and height 5 cm?
questions.explanation: V = πr²h = π × 9 × 5 = 45π cm³.

questions.question: What is the value of sin 30°?
questions.explanation: sin 30° = 1/2 is a special-angle value worth memorizing. (√3/2 is sin 60°; √2/2 is sin 45°.)

questions.question: A 13-meter ladder leans against a wall. Its foot is 5 meters from the wall. How high up the wall does the ladder reach?
questions.explanation: The ladder is the hypotenuse: h² + 5² = 13², so h² = 169 − 25 = 144 and h = 12 m.

questions.question: What is the measure of each interior angle of a regular octagon?
questions.explanation: Sum of angles = (8 − 2) × 180° = 1080°. A regular octagon has 8 equal angles: 1080° ÷ 8 = 135°.

questions.question: What is the mode of 3, 5, 5, 7, 8, 5, 2?
questions.explanation: The mode is the most frequent value. 5 appears three times.

questions.question: A fair six-sided die is rolled. What is the probability of rolling a number greater than 4?
questions.explanation: Only 5 and 6 are greater than 4: 2 out of 6 = 1/3.

questions.question: Two fair coins are tossed. What is the probability that both land heads?
questions.explanation: The outcomes are HH, HT, TH, TT. Only HH works: 1/4. (Or 1/2 × 1/2 for independent events.)

questions.question: The mean of five numbers is 12. Four of them are 10, 14, 9 and 15. What is the fifth number?
questions.explanation: The total must be 5 × 12 = 60. The four known numbers add to 48, so the fifth is 60 − 48 = 12.

questions.question: In how many different ways can 4 students stand in a line?
questions.explanation: Order matters: 4! = 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24.

questions.question: A bag has 4 red and 6 blue balls. Two balls are drawn one after the other WITHOUT replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.explanation: First red: 4/10. Then 3 red remain out of 9: 3/9. Multiply: (4/10)(3/9) = 12/90 = 2/15. (4/25 would be WITH replacement.)

questions.question: A store buys an item for ₱250 and marks it up by 20%. What is the selling price?
questions.explanation: Markup = 20% of ₱250 = ₱50. Selling price = ₱250 + ₱50 = ₱300.

questions.question: The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 3 : 5. There are 40 students. How many are girls?
questions.explanation: There are 3 + 5 = 8 parts, and 40 ÷ 8 = 5 students per part. Girls: 5 × 5 = 25.

questions.question: The price of a notebook rose from ₱80 to ₱100. What is the percent increase?
questions.explanation: Percent change = (new − old) ÷ old = 20 ÷ 80 = 0.25 = 25%. (20% would wrongly divide by the new price.)

questions.question: Two cars leave the same place at the same time and drive in opposite directions at 50 km/h and 70 km/h. How far apart are they after 2 hours?
questions.explanation: Moving apart, their speeds add: 50 + 70 = 120 km/h. In 2 hours: 120 × 2 = 240 km.

questions.question: Ana can paint a room in 4 hours. Ben can paint the same room in 6 hours. How long will it take if they work together?
questions.explanation: Together they paint 1/4 + 1/6 = 5/12 of the room per hour, so the job takes 12/5 = 2.4 hours = 2 hours 24 minutes.

questions.question: ₱5,000 is deposited at 4% interest compounded once a year. How much is in the account after 2 years?
questions.explanation: After year 1: 5,000 × 1.04 = 5,200. After year 2: 5,200 × 1.04 = 5,408. (₱5,400 would be simple interest.)

questions.question: What is the derivative of f(x) = 7?
questions.explanation: A constant never changes, so its rate of change (derivative) is 0.

questions.question: What is the derivative of f(x) = 5x³?
questions.explanation: Power rule with a constant multiple: 5 × 3x² = 15x².

questions.question: Evaluate the limit as x → 3 of (2x + 1).
questions.explanation: Direct substitution works: 2(3) + 1 = 7.

questions.question: Evaluate the limit as x → 1 of (x² − 1) / (x − 1).
questions.explanation: Substitution gives 0/0, so factor: (x − 1)(x + 1)/(x − 1) = x + 1 for x ≠ 1. As x → 1, this approaches 2.

questions.question: What is the slope of the tangent line to y = x² at x = 3?
questions.explanation: The slope of the tangent is the derivative: y′ = 2x. At x = 3, y′ = 6. (9 is the y-value, not the slope.)

questions.question: A ball's height is h(t) = 20t − 5t² meters after t seconds. At what time does it reach its maximum height?
questions.explanation: At the top, the rate of change is 0: h′(t) = 20 − 10t = 0, so t = 2 seconds. (At 4 seconds the ball is back at height 0.)

questions.question: Which organelle is the main site of cellular respiration and ATP production?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria carry out most of cellular respiration, releasing energy as ATP.

questions.question: Which structure is found in plant cells but NOT in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a rigid cell wall. Animal cells have only a cell membrane. Both have mitochondria and ribosomes.

questions.question: Two pea plants that are both heterozygous for height (Tt × Tt) are crossed. Tall (T) is dominant. What fraction of the offspring are expected to be short?
questions.explanation: The Punnett square gives TT, Tt, Tt, tt. Only tt is short: 1 out of 4.

questions.question: What are the products of photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants use carbon dioxide, water and light to make glucose, releasing oxygen.

questions.question: A human body cell has 46 chromosomes. How many chromosomes does each cell produced by meiosis have?
questions.explanation: Meiosis halves the chromosome number, so sex cells have 23. Fertilization restores 46.

questions.question: An atom has an atomic number of 11 and a mass number of 23. How many neutrons does it have?
questions.explanation: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 23 − 11 = 12.

questions.question: Which of the following is a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Burning makes new substances (ash, carbon dioxide, water vapor). The others change only form or mixture, not the substances themselves.

questions.question: A solution has a pH of 3. It is:
questions.explanation: Any pH below 7 is acidic.

questions.question: Which coefficients balance this equation? __H₂ + __O₂ → __H₂O
questions.explanation: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O has 4 hydrogen and 2 oxygen atoms on each side.

questions.question: What type of bond forms when a metal transfers electrons to a nonmetal, as in sodium chloride (NaCl)?
questions.explanation: Transferring electrons creates oppositely charged ions that attract: an ionic bond. Covalent bonds share electrons.

questions.question: A car travels 120 km in 2 hours. What is its average speed?
questions.explanation: Speed = distance ÷ time = 120 km ÷ 2 h = 60 km/h.

questions.question: A net force of 20 N acts on a 4 kg object. What is its acceleration?
questions.explanation: a = F ÷ m = 20 N ÷ 4 kg = 5 m/s².

questions.question: Which of Newton's laws best explains why a rifle recoils (kicks back) when fired?
questions.explanation: The rifle pushes the bullet forward, and the bullet pushes the rifle backward with an equal and opposite force.

questions.question: A 2 kg ball moves at 3 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: KE = ½mv² = ½ × 2 × 3² = ½ × 2 × 9 = 9 J.

questions.question: A 12 V battery is connected to a 4 Ω resistor. What current flows?
questions.explanation: Ohm's law: I = V ÷ R = 12 V ÷ 4 Ω = 3 A.

questions.question: Which layer of the Earth is made mostly of liquid metal?
questions.explanation: The outer core is liquid iron and nickel. The inner core is solid because of the enormous pressure.

questions.question: What is the main cause of the seasons on Earth?

options.text: Earth's changing distance from the Sun

questions.explanation: Earth's tilted axis (about 23.5°) changes how directly sunlight hits each hemisphere during the year.

questions.question: Which type of rock forms when magma or lava cools and hardens?
questions.explanation: Igneous rocks (such as basalt and granite) form from cooled molten rock.

questions.question: What usually happens where an oceanic plate meets a continental plate at a convergent boundary?

options.text: The continental plate sinks beneath the oceanic plate.
The plates slide past each other with no vertical movement.
New crust forms as the plates move apart.
The denser oceanic plate sinks beneath the continental plate, often forming a trench and volcanoes.

questions.explanation: Oceanic crust is denser, so it subducts under the continental plate. This creates deep trenches and volcanic arcs.

questions.question: In which layer of the atmosphere does almost all weather occur?
questions.explanation: The troposphere is the lowest layer and holds most of the air's water vapor, so clouds and storms form there.

questions.question: What is the basic unit of life?
questions.explanation: The cell is the smallest unit that can carry out all life processes. Atoms are not alive; tissues and organs are made of cells.

questions.question: Which blood cells carry oxygen around the body?
questions.explanation: Red blood cells contain hemoglobin, which binds oxygen. White blood cells fight infection, and platelets help blood clot.

questions.question: In which part of a plant cell does photosynthesis take place?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which captures light energy for photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which organ system breaks down food and absorbs nutrients?
questions.explanation: The digestive system (mouth, stomach, intestines and others) breaks food down and absorbs nutrients into the blood.

questions.question: In the food chain grass → grasshopper → frog → snake, which organism is the primary consumer?
questions.explanation: Grass is the producer. The first organism that eats the producer, the grasshopper, is the primary consumer.

questions.question: In DNA, adenine (A) always pairs with which base?
questions.explanation: In DNA, A pairs with T and G pairs with C. Uracil replaces thymine only in RNA.

questions.question: A trait controlled by a recessive allele appears only when the organism's genotype is:
questions.explanation: A dominant allele hides a recessive one, so the recessive trait shows only when both alleles are recessive.

questions.question: A heterozygous tall pea plant (Tt) is crossed with a short plant (tt). What percentage of the offspring are expected to be tall?
questions.explanation: The Punnett square gives Tt, Tt, tt, tt. Half have at least one T (tall): 50%.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
questions.explanation: Sodium's symbol, Na, comes from its Latin name, natrium. S is sulfur and N is nitrogen.

questions.question: Which state of matter has a definite volume but takes the shape of its container?
questions.explanation: A liquid keeps its volume but flows to fit its container. A solid keeps its shape; a gas fills any container.

questions.question: Which of these is a compound?
questions.explanation: A compound has two or more DIFFERENT elements chemically bonded. CO₂ contains carbon and oxygen. O₂ has only oxygen, so it is an element.

questions.question: How many electrons does a neutral oxygen atom (atomic number 8) have?
questions.explanation: Atomic number 8 means 8 protons, and a neutral atom has equal protons and electrons: 8.

questions.question: Which group of the periodic table contains the noble gases, such as neon and argon?
questions.explanation: The noble gases are in Group 18. Group 1 holds the alkali metals and Group 17 the halogens.

questions.question: What is the molar mass of carbon dioxide (CO₂)? (C = 12 g/mol, O = 16 g/mol)
questions.explanation: One carbon plus two oxygens: 12 + 2(16) = 44 g/mol.

questions.question: How many moles are in 36 g of water (H₂O, molar mass 18 g/mol)?
questions.explanation: moles = mass ÷ molar mass = 36 ÷ 18 = 2 mol.

questions.question: Which change makes a solution MORE acidic?
questions.explanation: A lower pH means more acidic. Only the change from 5 to 2 lowers the pH (about 1,000 times more acidic).

questions.question: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons (N). Joules measure energy, watts measure power, and pascals measure pressure.

questions.question: What is the weight of a 10 kg object on Earth? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.explanation: W = mg = 10 kg × 9.8 m/s² = 98 N. Mass (kg) and weight (N) are different quantities.

questions.question: A car speeds up from rest (0 m/s) to 20 m/s in 5 seconds. What is its average acceleration?
A 50 N force pushes a box 4 m in the direction of the force. How much work is done?
questions.explanation: Work = force × distance = 50 N × 4 m = 200 J.

questions.question: A 2 kg book rests on a shelf 1.5 m above the floor. What is its gravitational potential energy relative to the floor? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
Which color of visible light has the longest wavelength?
questions.explanation: In the visible spectrum (ROYGBIV), red has the longest wavelength and violet the shortest.

questions.question: Two 6 Ω resistors are connected in parallel. What is their total (equivalent) resistance?
questions.explanation: For parallel resistors: 1/R = 1/6 + 1/6 = 2/6, so R = 3 Ω. (12 Ω would be in series.)

questions.question: Which star is closest to Earth?
questions.explanation: The Sun is a star and by far the closest one to Earth. The Moon is not a star.

questions.question: Which layer of the atmosphere contains the ozone layer?
questions.explanation: The ozone layer, which absorbs much of the Sun's ultraviolet radiation, is in the stratosphere.

questions.question: What type of rock forms when existing rock is changed by heat and pressure?
questions.explanation: Metamorphic rocks (such as marble from limestone) form when heat and pressure change existing rock without melting it.

questions.question: Which instrument records ground shaking during an earthquake?
questions.explanation: A seismograph records seismic waves. Barometers measure air pressure, anemometers wind speed, and hygrometers humidity.

questions.question: During a lunar eclipse, which body is between the Sun and the Moon?
questions.explanation: In a lunar eclipse, Earth lies between the Sun and the Moon, and its shadow falls on the Moon. (In a solar eclipse, the Moon is between the Sun and Earth.)

questions.question: What is the difference between an earthquake's magnitude and its intensity?

options.text: They mean exactly the same thing.
Intensity measures energy released; magnitude describes the damage.
Magnitude applies only to volcanic eruptions.
Magnitude measures the energy released; intensity describes how strongly it is felt at a place.

questions.explanation: One earthquake has one magnitude (energy at the source), but its intensity varies by location, usually weaker farther from the epicenter.

questions.question: Why is it summer in the Southern Hemisphere when it is winter in the Northern Hemisphere?

options.text: The Southern Hemisphere is much closer to the Sun.
The Sun gives off more heat in those months.
The Southern Hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun at that time.
The Moon blocks sunlight from the Northern Hemisphere.

questions.explanation: Earth's tilted axis points one hemisphere toward the Sun while the other points away, so the seasons are opposite.

questions.question: Solve for x: 3^(2x − 1) = 27^(x + 2).
questions.explanation: Write 27 as 3³: 3^(2x − 1) = 3^(3x + 6). Set the exponents equal: 2x − 1 = 3x + 6, so x = −7.

questions.question: What is the domain of the real-valued function f(x) = √(x² − 16)?
questions.explanation: The expression under the square root must not be negative: x² − 16 ≥ 0, so x² ≥ 16. That gives x ≤ −4 or x ≥ 4.

questions.question: A parabola has its vertex at (1, −4) and passes through (3, 0). What is its equation in vertex form?
questions.explanation: Vertex form is y = a(x − h)² + k, so y = a(x − 1)² − 4. Plug in (3, 0): 0 = a(2)² − 4, so 4a = 4 and a = 1.

questions.question: A line has a slope of −3 and an x-intercept of 2. What is its y-intercept?
questions.explanation: The x-intercept is the point (2, 0). Point-slope form: y − 0 = −3(x − 2), so y = −3x + 6. The y-intercept is 6.

questions.question: Evaluate the limit as x approaches 3 of (x² − 9) / (x − 3).
questions.explanation: Factor: (x − 3)(x + 3) / (x − 3) = x + 3 when x ≠ 3. As x approaches 3, this approaches 3 + 3 = 6.

questions.question: In a triangle, side a = 5, side b = 8, and the included angle C = 60°. Use the Law of Cosines to find side c.
If log_b(3) = x and log_b(5) = y, express log_b(45) in terms of x and y.
Find the 8th term of the geometric sequence 2, −6, 18, −54, ...
How many different 4-letter arrangements can be formed from the letters of the word PHILIPPINES? (Each letter can be used only as many times as it appears.)
questions.explanation: PHILIPPINES has 3 P's, 3 I's, and one each of H, L, N, E, S (7 different letters). Count by case: all 4 different = 7 × 6 × 5 × 4 = 840; one letter used twice = 2 × C(6,2) × 12 = 360; P, P, I, I = 6; one letter used three times = 2 × 6 × 4 = 48. Total = 840 + 360 + 6 + 48 = 1,254.

questions.question: Two cards are drawn at the same time from a standard 52-card deck. What is the probability that both are aces?
Find the midpoint of the segment joining (−3, 5) and (7, −1).
A car travels at 60 km/h for 45 minutes and then at 80 km/h for 15 minutes. What is its average speed for the whole 1-hour trip?
questions.explanation: Distance = 60 × 0.75 + 80 × 0.25 = 45 + 20 = 65 km. Total time is 1 hour, so the average speed is 65 km/h. (Do not just average 60 and 80.)

questions.question: Which cell transport mechanism uses energy (ATP) to move substances against their concentration gradient?
questions.explanation: Active transport spends ATP to pump substances from low to high concentration. Diffusion and osmosis are passive and need no energy.

questions.question: What type of bond forms when valence electrons are shared unequally between two atoms because of a difference in electronegativity?
questions.explanation: In a polar covalent bond, electrons are shared but pulled more toward the more electronegative atom. In an ionic bond, electrons are transferred.

questions.question: An object starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 4.0 m/s² in a straight line. How far does it travel in 5.0 seconds?
questions.explanation: d = vᵢt + ½at². Since vᵢ = 0, d = ½ × 4.0 × 5² = 2 × 25 = 50 m.

questions.question: Which layer of the Earth is liquid and produces the planet's magnetic field through moving currents of iron and nickel?
questions.explanation: The outer core is molten iron and nickel. Its flowing currents act like a dynamo that creates Earth's magnetic field. The inner core is solid.

questions.question: What is the main role of the hormone insulin in the human body?

options.text: To raise blood glucose by breaking down glycogen
To help cells take in glucose, lowering blood glucose
To break down fats in fat tissue
To raise metabolic rate by stimulating the thyroid

questions.explanation: Insulin, made by the pancreas, helps cells absorb glucose, which lowers blood sugar. Glucagon does the opposite (raises blood sugar).

questions.question: Equal masses of water, aluminum, copper, and gold absorb the same amount of heat. Which one has the greatest temperature increase? (Specific heat: water > aluminum > copper > gold)
questions.explanation: From q = mcΔT, ΔT = q / (mc). With the same q and m, the substance with the lowest specific heat (gold) heats up the most.

questions.question: Which gas law states that at constant pressure, the volume of a gas is directly proportional to its absolute (Kelvin) temperature?
questions.explanation: Charles's Law: V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂ at constant pressure. Boyle's Law relates pressure and volume; Gay-Lussac's relates pressure and temperature.

questions.question: In an ecosystem, which organisms form the base of the food pyramid by turning energy from sunlight (or chemicals) into food?
questions.explanation: Primary producers (plants, algae, some bacteria) make their own food, so all other levels depend on them.

questions.question: A light ray passes at an angle from air into glass, which has a higher refractive index. What happens to its speed and direction?

options.text: It speeds up and bends away from the normal.
It slows down and bends toward the normal.
It slows down and bends away from the normal.
Its speed stays the same but it changes direction.

questions.explanation: Light slows down in a denser (higher index) medium and bends toward the normal line. Going the other way, it speeds up and bends away.

questions.question: Isotopes of the same element differ in the number of which particle?
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same number of protons (so they are the same element) but different numbers of neutrons, giving different mass numbers.

questions.question: What type of plate boundary formed the Himalayan mountain range?
questions.explanation: The Indian and Eurasian continental plates collided. Neither sank easily, so the crust crumpled and was pushed up into the Himalayas.

questions.question: Which functional group is found in all carboxylic acids?
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids (like acetic acid in vinegar) are defined by the carboxyl group, −COOH.

questions.question: Which sentence has correct pronoun-antecedent agreement in formal writing?

options.text: Every applicant must bring their original diploma to the office.
Each student must submit his or her credentials before the deadline.
The committee published their findings after weeks of verification.
Someone left their keys on the library counter yesterday.

questions.explanation: In strict formal grammar, singular words like each, every, and someone take singular pronouns (his or her). A committee acting as one unit takes its.

questions.question: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: The professor's explanation was so ________ that even beginning students understood the complex theory at once.
questions.explanation: Lucid means clear and easy to understand, which matches students understanding at once. Obscure and ambiguous mean unclear; pedantic means fussy about small details.

questions.question: Which sentence has correct parallel structure?

options.text: The internship offers valuable training, competitive stipends, and networking.
The internship offers valuable training, competitive stipends, and provides networking opportunities.
The internship offers training that is valuable, stipends that are competitive, and networks.
The internship offers valuable training, provides competitive stipends, and networking.

questions.explanation: All three items are nouns that complete "offers": training, stipends, networking. The other choices mix nouns and verbs.

questions.question: What is the main error in this sentence? "Running down the hallway, the flower vase was accidentally knocked over by Mark."
questions.explanation: The opening phrase "Running down the hallway" should describe the subject, but the subject is the vase. Mark was running, so the modifier dangles.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: The sudden drop in interest rates had an immediate ________ on the local real estate market.
questions.explanation: After "an immediate" you need a noun meaning result: effect. Affect is usually a verb (to influence).

questions.question: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?

options.text: The lecture was long, however, the students stayed attentive.
The lecture was long; however, the students stayed attentive.
The lecture was long however; the students stayed attentive.
The lecture was long, however; the students stayed attentive.

questions.explanation: When "however" joins two complete sentences, put a semicolon before it and a comma after it.

questions.question: Change to active voice: "The annual report was meticulously audited by the senior financial consultant."

options.text: The senior financial consultant meticulously audited the annual report.
The annual report had been meticulously audited by the senior financial consultant.
Meticulously auditing, the senior financial consultant finished the report.
The senior financial consultant was auditing the annual report meticulously.

questions.explanation: In active voice the doer (the consultant) is the subject and comes before the verb (audited). The meaning and tense stay the same.

questions.question: What is the closest antonym (opposite) of "garrulous"?
questions.explanation: Garrulous means very talkative. Reticent means quiet and reserved. Loquacious and voluble are synonyms of garrulous.

questions.question:
Read the sentence:
"The proliferation of digital misinformation has severely compromised public trust in conventional journalistic enterprises."

What does the author imply?

options.text: Digital news is better than traditional journalism.
Public trust is falling because misinformation makes it harder to know what is true.
Traditional journalism is the main source of misinformation.
More news leads to immediate public clarity.

questions.explanation: The sentence says spreading misinformation has damaged trust in traditional news. It does not say digital news is better or that journalists caused it.

questions.question:
Read the sentence:
"The proliferation of digital misinformation has severely compromised public trust in conventional journalistic enterprises."

As used in the sentence, what does "proliferation" mean?
questions.explanation: Proliferation means a rapid increase in number or spread, like misinformation multiplying online.

questions.question: Which sentence uses verb tenses correctly?

options.text: By the time the rescue team arrived, the hikers already left the cave.
By the time the rescue team arrived, the hikers had already left the cave.
By the time the rescue team arrives, the hikers already left the cave.
By the time the rescue team had arrived, the hikers will leave the cave.

questions.explanation: The past perfect (had left) shows an action finished before another past action (arrived).

questions.question: SCALPEL : SURGEON :: BRUSH : ___
questions.explanation: A scalpel is the tool a surgeon uses; a brush is the tool a painter uses (tool to user).

questions.question: In a code, TOKEN is written as VQMGP. How is SHIRT written in the same code?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves forward 2 places (T→V, O→Q, K→M, E→G, N→P). So S→U, H→J, I→K, R→T, T→V: UJKTV.

questions.question: Six people (A, B, C, D, E, F) sit in a row. B sits exactly between A and C. E sits immediately to the right of C. D sits to the left of A. F sits to the left of D. Who sits at the right end?
questions.explanation: Build it left to right: F, D, A, B, C, E. E is at the right end.

questions.question: Which word does NOT belong? Obdurate, Obstinate, Intractable, Pliant
questions.explanation: Obdurate, obstinate, and intractable all mean stubborn. Pliant means flexible and easily influenced, the opposite.

questions.question: A traveler drives 5 km west, turns left and drives 12 km, then turns left again and drives 5 km. How far is the traveler from the starting point?
questions.explanation: West 5, then left (south) 12, then left (east) 5. The east-west moves cancel, leaving the traveler 12 km south of the start.

questions.question: What comes next? B2, D4, F8, H16, ___
questions.explanation: Letters skip one (B, D, F, H, J) and numbers double (2, 4, 8, 16, 32). Next is J32.

questions.question: Premise 1: All mammals have mammary glands. Premise 2: A whale has mammary glands. Conclusion: Therefore, a whale is a mammal. Is this argument logically valid?

options.text: Valid, because the conclusion is biologically true.
Invalid, because it affirms the consequent.
Valid, because whales live in the ocean.
Invalid, because all mammals live on land.

questions.explanation: "All M have G" does not mean "everything with G is an M". The form is invalid (affirming the consequent) even though the conclusion happens to be true.

questions.question: A 4 × 4 × 4 cm wooden cube is painted on all outside faces, then cut into 1 × 1 × 1 cm cubes. How many small cubes have no paint at all?
questions.explanation: Unpainted cubes form the inner core, which is (4 − 2) × (4 − 2) × (4 − 2) = 2³ = 8 cubes.

questions.question: If 5 workers can build 5 tables in 5 days, how many days will it take 50 workers to build 50 tables at the same rate?
questions.explanation: Each worker builds 1 table in 5 days. With 50 workers, 50 tables also take 5 days.

questions.question: Solve for x: log₂(x − 1) + log₂(x + 2) = 2.
questions.explanation: Combine: log₂[(x − 1)(x + 2)] = 2, so x² + x − 2 = 4 and x² + x − 6 = 0, giving (x + 3)(x − 2) = 0. Reject x = −3 because it makes the logarithm's input negative. Only x = 2 works.

questions.question: A cylinder's height is twice its radius (h = 2r). If its volume is 54π cm³, what is the radius?
questions.explanation: V = πr²h = πr²(2r) = 2πr³ = 54π, so r³ = 27 and r = 3 cm.

questions.question: Anna can finish a project in 6 hours; Ben can finish it in 4 hours. How long will it take if they work together?
questions.explanation: Add the rates: 1/6 + 1/4 = 5/12 of the job per hour. Time = 12/5 = 2.4 hours.

questions.question: What is the sum of the infinite geometric series 12 − 4 + 4/3 − 4/9 + ...?
Which cell structure is mainly responsible for making lipids, metabolizing carbohydrates, and detoxifying drugs and poisons?
questions.explanation: The smooth ER (no ribosomes) makes lipids and breaks down toxins. The rough ER (with ribosomes) helps make proteins.

questions.question: What is the mass percent of oxygen in water (H₂O)? (H = 1 g/mol, O = 16 g/mol)
questions.explanation: Molar mass of H₂O = 2(1) + 16 = 18 g/mol. Oxygen % = 16/18 × 100% ≈ 88.9%.

questions.question: A ball is thrown straight up at 20 m/s. Ignoring air resistance, what maximum height does it reach? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: At the top, v = 0. Use v² = u² − 2gh: 0 = 400 − 20h, so h = 20 m.

questions.question: Which type of plate boundary has plates sliding horizontally past each other, causing earthquakes without creating or destroying crust?
questions.explanation: At transform boundaries (like the San Andreas Fault) plates slide past each other. Divergent boundaries create crust; convergent ones destroy it.

questions.question: Which sentence is grammatically correct?

options.text: Every boy and girl in the auditorium is required to submit an essay.
Each of the candidates have stated their platform clearly.
The news are very alarming this quarter.
Mathematics are my favorite subject in high school.

questions.explanation: Subjects introduced by every or each take a singular verb, even when joined by and. "Each ... have" should be has; news and mathematics are singular.

questions.question: What is the closest meaning of "ephemeral"?

options.text: Lasting for a very long time
Lasting for a very short time

questions.explanation: Ephemeral means short-lived or fleeting, like a rainbow.

questions.question:
Read the sentence:
"Despite the prevailing economic recession, the tech startup experienced an unprecedented surge in user acquisition, primarily driven by its innovative remote-collaboration tools."

What is the main implication?

options.text: Tech startups always succeed regardless of the economy.
Recessions are good for all digital companies.
Well-targeted innovation can create demand even in a hard economy.
Remote tools lose value during a recession.

questions.explanation: "Despite" signals contrast: the company grew in a bad economy because of its innovative tools. Avoid extreme choices like always or all.

questions.question: Which sentence has correct parallel structure?

options.text: She likes hiking, to swim, and reading books.
The manager wanted an assistant who is punctual, efficient, and demonstrates loyalty.
To succeed in college requires discipline, focus, and being adaptable.
The research paper must be thoroughly researched, clearly written, and properly cited.

questions.explanation: All three items share the same form (adverb + past participle): thoroughly researched, clearly written, properly cited.

questions.question: OMNIVOROUS : MEAT AND PLANTS :: HERBIVOROUS : ___
questions.explanation: An omnivore eats meat and plants; a herbivore eats plants only.

questions.question: What number comes next? 3, 6, 12, 24, 48, ___
questions.explanation: Each term is multiplied by 2: 48 × 2 = 96.

questions.question: All engineers are analytical. Some analytical people are creative. Based only on these statements, which conclusion is valid?

options.text: Some engineers may or may not be creative.

questions.explanation: The creative analytical people may or may not include engineers, so nothing definite can be said about engineers being creative.

questions.question: Find y in the system: 2x − 3y = 7 and 4x + y = 7.
questions.explanation: Multiply the second equation by 3: 12x + 3y = 21. Add to the first: 14x = 28, so x = 2. Then 4(2) + y = 7, so y = −1.

questions.question: If sin θ = 5/13 and θ is in Quadrant II, what is tan θ?
questions.explanation: Opposite = 5, hypotenuse = 13, so adjacent = √(169 − 25) = 12. tan θ = 5/12, but tangent is negative in Quadrant II: −5/12.

questions.question: Find the sum and product of the roots of 3x² − 6x + 2 = 0.
questions.explanation: For ax² + bx + c = 0: sum = −b/a = 6/3 = 2, product = c/a = 2/3.

questions.question: A council must choose a president, a vice president, and a secretary from 7 candidates. In how many ways can the positions be filled?
questions.explanation: The positions are different, so order matters (permutation): P(7, 3) = 7 × 6 × 5 = 210.

questions.question: What is the equation of the line through (2, −3) that is perpendicular to y = 2x + 5?
questions.explanation: A perpendicular slope is the negative reciprocal: −½. Then y + 3 = −½(x − 2), so y = −½x + 1 − 3 = −½x − 2.

questions.question: Simplify completely: (8x⁶ / y⁻³)^(1/3)
questions.explanation: 8x⁶ / y⁻³ = 8x⁶y³. Taking the cube root: 2 · x² · y = 2x²y.

questions.question: A bag has 4 red, 5 blue, and 3 green marbles. Two are drawn one after the other without replacement. What is the probability both are blue?
What is the 15th term of the arithmetic sequence 5, 11, 17, 23, ...?
What is the measure of each interior angle of a regular hexagon?
questions.explanation: Sum of interior angles = (6 − 2) × 180° = 720°. Each of the 6 equal angles is 720° ÷ 6 = 120°.

questions.question: What is the remainder when P(x) = x³ − 2x² + 4x − 5 is divided by (x − 2)?
questions.explanation: By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder is P(2) = 8 − 8 + 8 − 5 = 3.

questions.question: The mean score of 4 students is 85. When a 5th student's score is added, the mean becomes 82. What did the 5th student score?
questions.explanation: Sum of 4 scores = 4 × 85 = 340. Sum of 5 scores = 5 × 82 = 410. The 5th score is 410 − 340 = 70.

questions.question: How many liters of a 20% acid solution must be mixed with 4 liters of a 50% acid solution to make a 30% acid solution?
In pea plants, tall (T) is dominant over short (t). If a heterozygous tall plant (Tt) is crossed with a short plant (tt), what is the expected ratio of offspring?
questions.explanation: Tt × tt gives Tt, Tt, tt, tt: half tall and half short, a 1 : 1 ratio.

questions.question: In 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, how many moles of water form when 4.0 moles of H₂ react with excess oxygen?
questions.explanation: H₂ and H₂O are in a 2 : 2 (1 : 1) ratio, so 4.0 mol H₂ makes 4.0 mol H₂O.

questions.question: A 5.0 kg box on a frictionless floor is pushed with a net force of 15 N. What is its acceleration?
Which layer of the atmosphere contains the ozone layer that absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation?
questions.explanation: The ozone layer is in the stratosphere, just above the troposphere where weather happens.

questions.question: In an energy pyramid, about what percentage of energy at one trophic level is passed to the next level?
questions.explanation: The 10% rule: most energy is lost as heat or used for life processes, so only about 10% moves up a level.

questions.question: Moving left to right across a period of the periodic table, what generally happens to atomic radius and electronegativity?
questions.explanation: More protons pull the electrons closer (smaller radius) and attract bonding electrons more strongly (higher electronegativity).

questions.question: A 2.0 kg book is lifted from the floor onto a desk 1.5 m high. By how much does its gravitational potential energy increase? (g = 10 m/s²)
What type of rock forms when molten magma or lava cools and hardens?
questions.explanation: Igneous rocks form from cooled magma or lava. Sedimentary rocks form from layers of sediment; metamorphic rocks are changed by heat and pressure.

questions.question: Muscle cells need a constant supply of ATP. Which organelle is found in large numbers in muscle cells to supply it?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce ATP through cellular respiration, so very active cells like muscle cells have many of them. Animal cells have no chloroplasts.

questions.question: Which change increases the solubility of a solid solute (like sugar) in a liquid (like water)?
questions.explanation: For most solids, higher temperature means more sugar can dissolve. Stirring only makes it dissolve faster; pressure mainly affects gases.

questions.question: An object is placed beyond the focal point of a concave mirror. What kind of image is formed?
questions.explanation: Beyond the focal point, reflected rays meet in front of the mirror, forming a real, upside-down image. Inside the focal point you get a virtual, upright image.

questions.question: Solution A has pH 3.0 and Solution B has pH 6.0. How many times more acidic is A than B?
questions.explanation: The pH scale is base-10 logarithmic. A difference of 3 pH units means 10³ = 1,000 times more acidic.

questions.question: Which sentence does NOT contain a dangling or misplaced modifier?

options.text: Walking down the street, the bright sign caught her eye.
To win the championship, intensive training must be done every day.
While reading a classic novel, the electricity suddenly went out.
While reading a classic novel, she noticed the electricity suddenly go out.

questions.explanation: The opening phrase must describe the subject that follows. Only "she" can be reading the novel; the sign, the training, and the electricity cannot.

questions.question: "The CEO decided to call off the merger because the companies could not agree on leadership terms." What does "call off" mean?
questions.explanation: To call off means to cancel. To put off means to postpone.

questions.question: Which sentence shows correct pronoun agreement in formal writing?

options.text: Neither the choir members nor the conductor brought their sheet music.
Neither the choir members nor the conductor brought his or her sheet music.
Every student in the lab must submit their own report by noon.
The pack of wolves tracked their prey through the valley.

questions.explanation: With neither/nor, the pronoun agrees with the nearer noun. "Conductor" is singular, so use his or her.

questions.question: "Her performance in the debate was impeccable, leaving no room for her opponents to find flaws." What is a synonym for "impeccable"?
questions.explanation: Impeccable means without fault, which the sentence supports (no flaws to find).

questions.question: By the time the professor arrives next Monday, the student assistants ________ setting up the lab equipment.
questions.explanation: The future perfect (will have finished) shows an action completed before another future event.

questions.question: The structural changes had a profound ________ on student performance across the campus.
questions.explanation: After "a profound" you need a noun meaning result: effect.

questions.question: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?

options.text: The itinerary includes three stops, Tokyo, Japan, Paris, France, and Rome, Italy.
The itinerary includes three stops: Tokyo, Japan; Paris, France; and Rome, Italy.
The itinerary includes three stops; Tokyo, Japan, Paris, France, and Rome, Italy.
The itinerary includes three stops: Tokyo, Japan, Paris, France and Rome, Italy.

questions.explanation: A colon introduces the list. Because each item already contains a comma, semicolons separate the items.

questions.question: Which sentence is in the active voice?

options.text: The research data was carefully examined by the analytics team.
A mistake was made during the final step of the experiment.
The senior project manager approved the budget revisions yesterday.
The trophy will be presented by the league commissioner tonight.

questions.explanation: In active voice the subject does the action: the manager approved. The others use a form of "be" + past participle (passive).

questions.question:
Read the passage:
"The concept of cognitive reserve suggests that individuals who engage in mentally stimulating activities throughout their lives develop a resilience to neuropathological damage. While structural changes associated with cognitive decline, such as brain atrophy or the accumulation of amyloid plaques, may still occur, individuals with high cognitive reserve can utilize alternative neural networks to maintain functional capacity. Consequently, tracking an individual's educational level, occupational complexity, and social engagement offers far more accurate prognostic insight into their daily functional longevity than relying solely on direct neuroimaging metrics."

According to the passage, what does cognitive reserve allow a person to do?

options.text: Prevent all brain damage and atrophy
Keep functioning day to day by using alternative neural pathways

questions.explanation: The passage says damage may still occur, but people with high reserve use alternative neural networks to keep functioning.

questions.question:
Read the passage:
"The concept of cognitive reserve suggests that individuals who engage in mentally stimulating activities throughout their lives develop a resilience to neuropathological damage. While structural changes associated with cognitive decline, such as brain atrophy or the accumulation of amyloid plaques, may still occur, individuals with high cognitive reserve can utilize alternative neural networks to maintain functional capacity. Consequently, tracking an individual's educational level, occupational complexity, and social engagement offers far more accurate prognostic insight into their daily functional longevity than relying solely on direct neuroimaging metrics."

What does the passage imply about neuroimaging (brain scans)?

options.text: They are useless for older patients.
They predict daily functioning less accurately than lifestyle factors do.
They always conflict with a person's education level.
They are cheaper than studying lifestyle history.

questions.explanation: The last sentence says education, job complexity, and social life give more accurate insight than scans alone. It does not call scans useless.

questions.question:
Read the passage:
"The concept of cognitive reserve suggests that individuals who engage in mentally stimulating activities throughout their lives develop a resilience to neuropathological damage. While structural changes associated with cognitive decline, such as brain atrophy or the accumulation of amyloid plaques, may still occur, individuals with high cognitive reserve can utilize alternative neural networks to maintain functional capacity. Consequently, tracking an individual's educational level, occupational complexity, and social engagement offers far more accurate prognostic insight into their daily functional longevity than relying solely on direct neuroimaging metrics."

As used in the passage, what does "prognostic" mean?

options.text: Predicting a future outcome or course

questions.explanation: A prognosis is a prediction of how something (like a health condition) will develop. Prognostic insight helps predict the future.

questions.question: What number comes next? 2, 5, 11, 23, 47, ___
questions.explanation: Each term is (previous × 2) + 1: 47 × 2 + 1 = 95.

questions.question: What letter comes next? J, F, M, A, M, J, J, ___
questions.explanation: These are the first letters of the months: January to July. August comes next.

questions.question: MIND : COGNITION :: HEART : ___
questions.explanation: The mind carries out cognition (thinking); the heart carries out circulation (pumping blood).

questions.question: Premise 1: All planets in our solar system orbit the Sun. Premise 2: Kepler-186f orbits a star that is not the Sun. Conclusion: Kepler-186f is not a planet in our solar system. Is the conclusion valid?

options.text: Valid only if Kepler-186f is larger than Earth
Cannot be decided without more data

questions.explanation: If it were a planet in our solar system, it would orbit the Sun. It does not, so it cannot be one. This is a valid form (denying the consequent).

questions.question: In a code, CAMPUS is written as EBOQWT. How is TIGER written in the same code?
questions.explanation: The shifts alternate +2, +1, +2, +1, ...: C→E, A→B, M→O, P→Q, U→W, S→T. For TIGER: T→V, I→J, G→I, E→F, R→T = VJIFT.

questions.question: A person walks 10 m north, turns right and walks 6 m, turns right again and walks 18 m, then turns right and walks 6 m. Where is the person now compared with the start?
questions.explanation: North 10, east 6, south 18, west 6. East and west cancel; 10 north − 18 south = 8 m south.

questions.question: Which word does NOT belong? Epiphany, Insight, Delusion, Realization
questions.explanation: Epiphany, insight, and realization all mean a true understanding. A delusion is a false belief.

questions.question: What comes next? AZ, CX, EV, GT, ___
questions.explanation: First letters go forward by 2 (A, C, E, G, I); second letters go backward by 2 (Z, X, V, T, R). Next is IR.

questions.question: Five runners (A, B, C, D, E) finish a race with no ties. A finished immediately ahead of B. D finished immediately ahead of A. C finished ahead of D. E did not finish in the top three. Who finished last?
questions.explanation: D, A, B must finish together in that order, and C is ahead of D. E is not in the top three, so the only order is C, D, A, B, E. E is last.

questions.question:
Is the integer x divisible by 6?
Statement 1: x is divisible by 2.
Statement 2: x is divisible by 3.
Which is true about the statements?

options.text: Both together are enough, but neither alone is.
Both together are still not enough.

questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 6 only if it is divisible by both 2 and 3. Each statement alone is not enough; together they are.

questions.question: Which sentence has correct subject-verb agreement?

options.text: The list of requirements are posted online.
The list of requirements is posted online.
The requirements list are posted online.
The list of requirement were posted online.

questions.explanation: The subject is "list" (singular), not "requirements", so the verb is "is".

questions.question: Which word best completes the sentence? The scientist remained ____ despite repeated criticism of her theory.
questions.explanation: Resilient means able to stay strong or recover despite difficulty, which fits "despite repeated criticism".

questions.question: Which sentence uses pronouns correctly in formal writing?

options.text: Each student must submit their form before noon.
Each student must submit his or her form before noon.
Each students must submit his form before noon.
Each student must submits their form before noon.

questions.explanation: In formal singular agreement, "each student" pairs with "his or her" and the base verb "submit".

questions.question: Read the statement: "Because the road was flooded, classes were suspended." What is the cause?
questions.explanation: "Because" introduces the cause: the flooding caused the suspension of classes.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the word "affect" correctly?

options.text: The new rule will affect attendance.
The new rule had a positive affect.
Attendance was an affect of the rule.

questions.explanation: Affect is usually a verb meaning to influence. The other sentences need the noun "effect".

questions.question: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?

options.text: After the exam we went, home.
After the exam, we went home.
After, the exam we went home.
After the exam we, went home.

questions.explanation: An introductory phrase like "After the exam" is normally followed by a comma.

questions.question: Choose the best synonym for "concise".
questions.explanation: Concise means brief but clear, saying a lot in few words.

questions.question: Which sentence is in the passive voice?

options.text: The proposal was approved by the committee.
The committee will review the proposal.

questions.explanation: In passive voice the receiver of the action (the proposal) is the subject: "was approved by".

questions.question: Which transition best completes the sentence? The first experiment failed; ____, the researchers revised their method and tried again.
questions.explanation: The revision happened as a result of the failure, so "therefore" (cause and effect) fits best.
